topic: Fall Prevention Month: staying steady on winter ice and at home
headline: Stay steady
intro: Icy sidewalks, dark evenings and some medicines can all affect your balance. Small habits help.

points.title: Dress for icy sidewalks
points.body: Wear boots with a good grip, take shorter steps, and hold the handrail on icy stairs and ramps.
points.tip: Keep salt or grit by your door.

points.title: Light up your home
points.body: Use night lights between the bedroom and bathroom, and keep floors and stairs clear.
points.tip: Tape down or remove loose rugs.

points.title: Check your medications
points.body: Some medicines can cause dizziness or drowsiness. Ask us if anything you take could affect your balance.

points.title: Think about bone health
points.body: Many Canadians get less sun in winter. Ask us if a vitamin D or calcium supplement fits your needs.

cta_body: Ask our pharmacist about a MedsCheck review.

caption_instagram:
4 ways to stay steady this winter ❄️🚶

November is Fall Prevention Month, and North York sidewalks are about to get icy. Our Toronto pharmacy team's quick checklist:
1️⃣ Wear boots with a good grip and take shorter steps on ice
2️⃣ Add night lights and clear clutter from floors and stairs
3️⃣ Some medicines can cause dizziness or drowsiness. Ask us if yours could affect your balance
4️⃣ Ask us whether a vitamin D or calcium supplement fits your needs this winter

Want a one-on-one review of your medications? Ask our pharmacist about a MedsCheck (ask if you're eligible).
